assets.name: Kozmino

assets.name: Rotterdam
assets.note: Pricing centre for north-west European products.

assets.name: Trieste
assets.note: Feeds Austria, southern Germany and Czechia by the Transalpine Pipeline.

assets.name: Gdansk Naftoport

assets.name: Corpus Christi port
assets.note: Largest United States crude export port.

assets.name: Louisiana Offshore Oil Port

assets.name: Cushing
assets.note: Delivery point for West Texas Intermediate futures. Inland.

assets.name: Vancouver Westridge
assets.note: End of Trans Mountain. Gave Canadian crude Pacific access in 2024.

assets.name: Acu
assets.capacity_text: About 25 percent of Brazilian crude exports

assets.name: Arzew port
assets.trade_role: Crude, LNG, liquefied petroleum gas export

assets.name: Walvis Bay
assets.note: Current logistics base for Orange Basin drilling.

assets.name: Luderitz
assets.capacity_text: Closest port to the Orange Basin
assets.note: Namport is developing an oil and gas supply base here. Shallow draft and limited land are the constraints.

assets.name: Mombasa port
assets.capacity_text: Main East African product import port

assets.name: Tanga
assets.capacity_text: End of the East African Crude Oil Pipeline
assets.note: Terminal under construction.

assets.name: Singapore
assets.capacity_text: Largest bunkering port in the world
assets.note: Asian pricing centre.

assets.name: Ningbo-Zhoushan
assets.capacity_text: Largest port in the world by tonnage

assets.name: Qingdao and Shandong ports
assets.note: Destination for most sanctioned Iranian, Russian and Venezuelan barrels.

assets.name: Duqm port
assets.note: Outside the Strait of Hormuz.

assets.name: Strait of Hormuz
assets.capacity_text: About 20 million barrels/day, plus about 20 percent of world LNG
assets.note: Most critical oil chokepoint. Bypass capacity is only about 2.6 million barrels/day. Closure threatened during the June 2025 Israel-Iran war.

assets.name: Strait of Malacca
assets.note: Busiest oil chokepoint by volume. Main route to China, Japan and South Korea.

assets.name: Suez Canal and SUMED
assets.capacity_text: About 9 million barrels/day in normal times
assets.note: Flows well below normal since Houthi attacks began in late 2023.

assets.name: Bab el-Mandeb
assets.capacity_text: About 4 million barrels/day currently, half of pre-2024
assets.note: Red Sea gateway. Most Western-linked tankers and nearly all LNG carriers still divert round the Cape.

assets.name: Turkish Straits
assets.note: Outlet for Russian and Kazakh Black Sea crude.

assets.name: Danish Straits
assets.note: Outlet for Russian Baltic crude. Shadow fleet scrutiny rising.

assets.name: Panama Canal
assets.capacity_text: About 2 million barrels/day, mostly products and liquefied petroleum gas
assets.note: Drought restrictions in 2023-24 pushed United States LNG to the Cape route. Many LNG carriers still avoid it.

assets.name: Cape of Good Hope
assets.capacity_text: About 9 million barrels/day, up sharply since 2024
assets.note: The diversion route when the Red Sea is unsafe. Adds 10 to 14 days to Asia-Europe voyages.

assets.name: Hoegh Gandria (Egypt, incoming)
assets.capacity_text: Hoegh Gandria, about 1 billion cubic feet/day peak
assets.note: Ten-year deployment agreed. Replaces short-term units and signals Egypt expects to import for a decade.

assets.name: Khor Al Zubair
assets.operator: Iraq Ministry of Electricity / Excelerate Energy
assets.note: Definitive agreement signed October 2025. Start-up slipped from 2026 to 2027 because of the regional conflict. Dredging under way in August 2026.
assets.charter_note: Five years renewable, with a minimum contracted offtake. Excelerate also supplies the LNG.
assets.source: Excelerate Energy, Iraqi News, Dredging Today

assets.name: Nador West Med
assets.note: Tender launched 2025. Would end reliance on reverse flow through Spain.
assets.charter_note: Tender stage.

assets.name: Jebel Ali
assets.note: Seasonal summer imports.
assets.charter_note: Extended several times. Current end date not known.

assets.name: Aliaga (Etki)
assets.charter_note: Not known.

assets.name: Acu (GNA)
assets.note: Feeds 3 gigawatts of gas-fired power at the port.
assets.charter_note: Twenty-three years from 2021.

assets.name: Bahia
assets.charter_note: Ten years from 2024.

assets.name: Lampung
assets.charter_note: Twenty years from 2014.

assets.name: West Java (Jakarta Bay)
assets.note: First FSRU in Asia, 2012.
assets.charter_note: Extended past the original 2022 end. Current end date not known.

assets.name: Kerawalapitiya
assets.note: Repeatedly re-tendered.
assets.charter_note: No vessel contracted.

assets.name: Taranaki
assets.note: Announced 2025 in response to declining domestic gas.
assets.charter_note: No vessel contracted.

assets.name: Beni Suef
assets.note: One of three Siemens mega-plants. Egypt needs roughly 60 billion cubic metres/year and produces well under that. The gap is filled by Israeli pipeline gas and LNG.

assets.name: Burullus
assets.note: Summer peak drives the LNG buying season.

assets.name: Samra and central Jordan plants
assets.note: About 85 percent of Jordanian power is gas-fired. Exposed whenever Israeli flows are cut.

assets.name: Deir Ammar and Zahrani
assets.note: Built for gas, never supplied. Floating terminal plans shelved several times. Supply through the Arab Gas Pipeline is the cheaper fix.

assets.name: Deir Ali and Syrian grid
assets.note: Reconstruction demand. Qatar-funded gas supply and 5 gigawatts of new plants agreed with a Turkish-Qatari-American group.

assets.name: Vasilikos power station
assets.operator: Fuel oil until the floating terminal starts
assets.note: Highest power prices in the European Union while the plant waits for gas.

assets.name: Basra and southern Iraq plants
assets.operator: Iranian pipeline gas, flared gas capture
assets.note: United States waiver for Iranian supply ended in 2025. Drives the floating terminal at Khor Al Zubair.

assets.name: Tahaddart and Ain Beni Mathar
assets.operator: LNG landed in Spain, reverse flow
assets.note: New Al Wahda gas plants planned. Demand case for the Nador terminal.

assets.name: Tunisian grid
assets.note: Over 95 percent gas-fired. Wholly dependent on Algeria.

assets.name: Cap des Biches and Dakar plants
assets.operator: Heavy fuel oil and LNG now. Domestic gas later
assets.note: West African Energy 366 megawatt combined-cycle plant started 2025. State plan converts the fleet to gas. Bridge period needs imported LNG.

assets.name: Abidjan plants (Azito, CIPREL, Atinkou)
assets.note: Earlier LNG import project shelved after the Baleine discovery.

assets.name: Tema and Takoradi enclaves
assets.operator: Domestic gas and West African Gas Pipeline
assets.note: Persistent gas payment arrears. Tema LNG idle beside it.

assets.name: Maria Gleta
assets.note: Unreliable Nigerian supply has kept a floating import option alive.

assets.name: Nigerian grid (Egbin, Azura and others)
assets.capacity_text: About 12 gigawatts installed, under half available
assets.note: Gas shortfalls and debts to suppliers strand capacity.

assets.name: Kudu and southern Namibia
assets.note: Namibia imports most of its power from South Africa.

assets.name: Richards Bay combined cycle
assets.note: Environmental approval overturned in court, then reinstated on appeal. Anchor demand for the Richards Bay terminal.

assets.name: Ankerlig and Gourikwa
assets.note: Burning diesel as peakers. Conversion needs an import terminal in the Western Cape.

assets.name: Gauteng industrial gas market
assets.note: Supply from Mozambique declines from about 2028. Known locally as the gas cliff. Industrial users, not power.

assets.name: Temane
assets.note: Commissioning. Largest new plant in Mozambique since independence.

assets.name: Kinyerezi, Dar es Salaam
assets.operator: Domestic Songo Songo and Mnazi Bay gas

assets.name: Mombasa LNG-to-power
assets.note: Floated repeatedly. Geothermal keeps crowding it out.

assets.name: Algerian domestic demand
assets.note: Domestic use now rivals export volume. The main long-term threat to Algerian supply to Europe.

assets.name: Libyan grid
assets.note: Summer shortages cut Greenstream exports to Italy.

assets.name: Sonker liquid bulk terminal, Ain Sokhna
assets.capacity_text: 100,000 cubic metres gasoil and 150,000 cubic metres LPG storage, plus FSRU berths
assets.operator: Sonker Bunkering Company (Egyptian Amiral Petroleum Services 51 percent; Misr Petroleum 15; Suez Canal Economic Zone authority 12; Ministry of Finance 12; Petroleum Cooperative 10)
assets.trade_role: LPG, gasoil and LNG import; ammonia export
assets.note: Basin 3 of Sokhna Port, under an agreement with DP World Sokhna. Completed 2020. Hosts the berths where Egypt's floating LNG terminals dock. 25-year supply point agreement with EGPC. Gasoil pipeline of 37.5 kilometres to the national grid. Original project cost about 417 million dollars; a refinancing of up to 355 million dollars was disclosed in 2022 and is still listed as pending.
assets.source: International Finance Corporation project disclosures 36828 and 44905; EBRD

assets.name: Ain Sokhna onshore LNG terminal (tender)
assets.capacity_text: About 1 billion cubic feet/day initially, with floating storage of up to 290,000 cubic metres
assets.note: Egypt's first permanent regasification terminal. Three bidders reported in August 2026: BGN of Turkey, UCC Holding of Qatar and a local player. Cost, award date and construction timing not disclosed. Would reduce reliance on leased floating units.

routes.name: Druzhba

routes.name: Eastern Siberia-Pacific Ocean

routes.name: Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan
routes.capacity_text: 1.2 million barrels/day design, runs about half
routes.note: Carries Azeri crude, plus some Kazakh and Turkmen volumes.

routes.note: Carries over 80 percent of Kazakh exports across Russia. Pump stations hit by drones in 2025.

routes.name: Kirkuk-Ceyhan
routes.note: Restarted September 2025 after a two and a half year shutdown. Volumes still modest.

routes.name: East-West Pipeline (Petroline)
routes.note: Saudi bypass of the Strait of Hormuz.

routes.name: Habshan-Fujairah
routes.note: Abu Dhabi bypass of the Strait of Hormuz.

routes.name: SUMED
routes.note: Links Red Sea to Mediterranean for tankers too large for the Suez Canal.

routes.name: Goreh-Jask
routes.capacity_text: About 1 million barrels/day design, lightly used

routes.name: Basra-Aqaba
routes.note: Proposed for over a decade. No financing.

routes.name: Keystone

routes.name: Enbridge Mainline

routes.name: Trans Mountain

routes.name: Colonial (refined products)

routes.name: East African Crude Oil Pipeline

routes.name: Niger-Benin

routes.name: Kazakhstan-China
routes.note: Also carries Russian crude in transit.

routes.name: Baltic Pipeline System

routes.name: Transalpine Pipeline

routes.name: Vaca Muerta Oil Sur

routes.name: Nord Stream 1 and 2

routes.name: Yamal-Europe
routes.note: Idle for Russian gas since 2022. Polish section runs in reverse.

routes.name: Ukraine transit corridor

routes.name: TurkStream

routes.name: Power of Siberia

routes.name: Power of Siberia 2

routes.name: Central Asia-China

routes.name: West-East Gas Pipelines

routes.name: EastMed

routes.name: West African Gas Pipeline

routes.name: Dolphin

routes.name: Transco

routes.name: Coastal GasLink
routes.note: Feeds LNG Canada.

routes.name: Gulf to Europe via the Cape (diversion)

news.headline: Petrobras extends Excelerate Sequoia FSRU contract to 2038
news.summary: August agreement adds five years to the Sequoia charter, to 2038; a reliquefaction unit is to be fitted at the 2028 dry dock, with a modest revenue uplift from 2028.

news.headline: Excelerate guides Iraq terminal start-up to second quarter 2027 as jetty materials arrive
news.summary: Third-quarter release: jetty materials arriving, workforce on site, an FSRU already in the region will avoid a Hormuz transit; minimum offtake 250 million cubic feet/day (as reported).

news.headline: Excelerate says new Jordan charter lifted third-quarter earnings
news.summary: Company attributes the sequential rise in results to its new Jordan charter and says the Iraq terminal will be served by an FSRU already positioned in the region.

news.headline: Energos Winter still in Spain for repairs with no confirmed return date
news.summary: Enterprise notes the drone-damaged Energos Winter remains out of service and under repair in Spain, with no confirmed date for a return to Damietta.

news.headline: Egypt trims November LNG imports to about ten cargoes and lines up Hoegh Gandria for Ain Sokhna
news.summary: Egypt cut November import requests to about ten cargoes, deferred five contracted cargoes into 2027, and plans to swap Hoegh Galleon for Hoegh Gandria at Ain Sokhna in early December (as reported).

news.headline: Hoegh Gandria reported to replace Hoegh Galleon at Ain Sokhna in early December
news.summary: Enterprise reports the converted Hoegh Gandria, up to about 1 billion cubic feet/day, will take over the Ain Sokhna berth from Hoegh Galleon in early December 2026 under its ten-year charter.

news.headline: NNPC chief says AKK pipeline will deliver gas to Abuja before end of 2026
news.summary: Speaking at ADIPEC, the NNPC group chief executive said first gas to Abuja for power and industry is expected before year-end; management statement, deadlines have slipped before.

news.headline: Egypt and Chevron review Aphrodite tie-in agreements ahead of investment decision
news.summary: At ADIPEC the petroleum minister and Chevron discussed finalising agreements to link Aphrodite output to Egyptian infrastructure, described as paving the way for FID.

news.headline: Aramco says Jafurah phase two remains on track
news.summary: Third-quarter results list Jafurah phase two, the Fadhili gas plant expansion and Dammam among upstream projects on track; no new dates.

news.headline: Aramco reports production has started at the Zuluf crude increment
news.summary: Third-quarter results state that production commenced at the Zuluf increment; no date or volume given. Marjan and Berri are not mentioned.

news.headline: Stade FSRU terminal receives its first LNG cargo
news.summary: Deutsche Energy Terminal says the Energos Force-based Stade terminal has taken its first LNG cargo, with grid send-out expected to follow in November.

news.headline: Petrojet reported to win contract for onshore pipeline carrying Cypriot Cronos gas to Damietta
news.summary: Reported USD 170 million, roughly 40 km Port Said to Damietta line, about 12 months of work from early 2027; Cronos first gas guided first half 2028 (figures need verification).

news.headline: Qatari LNG tanker bound for Pakistan attacked near Hormuz
news.summary: Qatar and Saudi Arabia condemned an attack on a Qatar Gas Transport carrier reportedly carrying a Pakistan cargo; Qatar opened an investigation. Adds risk to winter supply.

news.headline: Algeria courts Russian firms for the Trans-Saharan gas pipeline
news.summary: Algeria's foreign minister said in Moscow on 27 October that talks are under way to bring Russian companies into the Nigeria-Niger-Algeria pipeline; no firm named, no contract signed.

news.headline: TotalEnergies chief says Mopane drilling is imminent
news.summary: TotalEnergies' chief executive told Semafor that drilling on the Mopane discovery, where it now operates, is about to start; page could not be read in full, headline only.

news.headline: Technip Energies says first North Field East train ready for handover to QatarEnergy
news.summary: Contractor CEO says train 1 is ready to hand over and train 2 has started commissioning; QatarEnergy has not confirmed a start-up date (paywalled, lede only).

news.headline: Australian environment minister declines to set timeline for Browse decision
news.summary: Minister Murray Watt gave no timeframe for approving or rejecting Browse; the department's final recommendation had been expected mid-to-late 2026.

news.headline: QatarEnergy extends Pakistan LNG force majeure to 29 December
news.summary: Pakistani officials say QatarEnergy's force majeure now runs to 29 December, raising winter shortfall risk; spot cargoes reported at several times normal cost (figures need verification).

news.headline: OMV Petrom shareholders to vote 6 November on higher 2026 capex, mainly for Neptun Deep
news.summary: Proposed increase of about 1 billion lei to roughly 10 billion lei (as reported); company reiterates first gas in first half 2027.

news.headline: Punta Colorada terminal takes shape with first crude export targeted for first quarter 2027
news.summary: Six 750,000-barrel tanks and two offshore monobuoys; only two tanks operational in the first stage; about 1,600 workers on site (as reported).

news.headline: SPEC terminal back to full 533 million cubic feet/day after single-train repair
news.summary: Rationing ran 27-31 October while one of four FSRU trains was repaired at about 400 million cubic feet/day; capacity reported back at 533 (figures as reported).

news.headline: Colombia lifts gas rationing after SPEC Cartagena terminal fault is fixed early
news.summary: Energy ministry ended the scheduled gas restriction at midnight on 31 October after SPEC LNG restored regasification capacity; repairs finished a day ahead of plan.

news.headline: TotalEnergies reaffirms 2028 first oil at GranMorgu; development drilling from early January
news.summary: TotalEnergies' Suriname manager said first oil stays 2028 with two rigs starting production drilling in early January 2027; government and operator progress figures differ (43 versus 50 percent, as reported).

news.headline: Third Qatari October cargo berths at Engro's Port Qasim terminal
news.summary: A third Qatari cargo in October berthed at the Engro terminal on 31 October (as reported), confirming the Exquisite unit is regasifying; no mention of the Pakistan GasPort unit.

news.headline: Eni asset swap doubles ExxonMobil's Rovuma interest; FID still targeted end-2026
news.summary: Reports the 25 to 50 percent increase came via an asset swap with Eni, with FID targeted by end-2026 and operations from 2031 (needs a second source on Eni).

news.headline: ExxonMobil expects Golden Pass train 2 substantially complete by December
news.summary: On its quarterly call ExxonMobil said train 2 should be substantially complete by December after contractor-bankruptcy delays, with lessons applied to train 3; single source, needs verification.

news.headline: NextDecade guides Rio Grande train 1 first LNG to second quarter 2027
news.summary: NextDecade expects feed gas before end-2026, first LNG from train 1 in second quarter 2027 and substantial completion in third quarter 2027, ahead of the contractor schedule; train 6 FID eyed second half 2027.

news.headline: ExxonMobil to lift Rovuma LNG stake to 50 percent
news.summary: ExxonMobil announced with third-quarter results that it will raise its Rovuma LNG working interest to 50 percent; it remains operator.

news.headline: MEES: Qatar's Lebanon power plan still lacks financing, pipeline and gas supply arrangements
news.summary: Analysis of the Qatari proposal for two 825 megawatt plants and an FSRU says financing, pipeline infrastructure and gas supply are unresolved.

news.headline: Egypt buys fuel oil for year-end as LNG prices climb; import cargo count set to rise
news.summary: EGPC bought six fuel oil cargoes for November-December; Egypt's LNG cargo count this year reported rising to 184 from 152 (figures need verification).

news.headline: YPF puts Vaca Muerta Oil Sur above 85 percent complete, line fill January, first ship March 2027
news.summary: Stage one 180 thousand barrels/day, full system 550 thousand, expansion to 750 thousand under study; three of six tanks finished (figures as reported).

news.headline: Neptun Deep platform installed, eight wells done, shore pipeline laid
news.summary: Nine-month results note the production platform is installed, eight wells completed and the pipeline to shore laid, with first gas targeted in 2027.

news.headline: OMV Petrom nine-month results keep Neptun Deep first gas in first half 2027
news.summary: Results published 28 October: record investment directed at Neptun Deep, with first gas still guided for the first half of 2027.

news.headline: BW Energy parks Kudu appraisal while farm-down process runs into 2027
news.summary: BW Energy says the Kudu farm-down data room has drawn wide interest, with phase two in early 2027 and closing including approvals in second half 2027; appraisal drilling stays on hold.

news.headline: Woodside signs 20-year Louisiana LNG supply deal with QatarEnergy
news.summary: Woodside will sell QatarEnergy up to 3 million tonnes a year (as reported) for 20 years, ramping with trains 2 and 3; first LNG still targeted 2029.

news.headline: TotalEnergies closes Galp deal for operated Mopane stake; next well about to spud
news.summary: TotalEnergies lists the closing of its 40 percent operated interest in PEL 83 (as reported); Galp separately said the Mopane 4X well is about to start and no further farm-down is planned.

news.headline: VMOS line fill due around year-end, first crude export targeted March 2027
news.summary: Pipeline and Punta Colorada tanks to start filling late December or January; first export around March 2027; initial 190 thousand barrels/day (as reported).

news.headline: VMOS reported 85 percent complete with a 40 to 50 day line fill ahead of March export
news.summary: Project put at 85 percent complete; fill from January takes 40-50 days; ramp 180 to 390 thousand barrels/day by mid-2027, 550 in 2028 (as reported).

news.headline: LNG Prime confirms MOL deal for second Mukran FSRU
news.summary: Second outlet reporting the Deutsche ReGas and MOL charter for a second floating unit to restore full capacity at Mukran; article body is paywalled.

news.headline: Deutsche ReGas signs long-term charter with MOL for a second Mukran FSRU from 2028
news.summary: MOL will convert an LNG carrier at Hudong-Zhonghua into an FSRU for Deutsche ReGas, on charter from 2028, restoring the terminal's fully permitted two-unit capacity.

news.headline: Equinor points to an early-2027 Bay du Nord investment decision with Shell on board
news.summary: Equinor bought bp's Bay du Nord interest, sold 30 percent to Shell in October and says it is moving towards an investment decision; the CFO put FID in early 2027 on the call.

news.headline: Energos Force cooling down in Rotterdam ahead of Stade start next month
news.summary: Terminal operator DET says the 174,000 cubic metre FSRU is cooling its tanks in Rotterdam and Stade operations begin in November 2026.

news.headline: SPEC outage removes roughly an eighth of Colombian gas supply during repairs
news.summary: Rationing began 27 October; reported capacity loss is about 75 to 133 million cubic feet/day depending on source, with no confirmed end date.

news.headline: Uganda reaffirms 60,000 barrels/day Hoima refinery with Alpha MBM
news.summary: Minister restates the plan for a roughly 4 billion dollar, up to 60,000 barrels/day refinery backed by Alpha MBM as the next infrastructure push after first oil (figures as reported).

news.headline: Uganda's energy minister targets Kingfisher first oil by end-2026
news.summary: Minister Monica Musenero told Platts that first oil from CNOOC's Kingfisher field is targeted for end-2026, after Hormuz-stranded equipment was airlifted in.

news.headline: Uganda guides first EACOP exports from Tanzania in early 2027
news.summary: Uganda's energy minister says crude exports through the pipeline to Tanga should begin in early 2027, consistent with earlier UNOC guidance.

news.headline: Inpex finishes Abadi FEED three months early; FID targeted around January 2027
news.summary: Indonesia's regulator says Abadi LNG front-end engineering finished in October, ahead of plan, with FID hoped for by late 2026 or January 2027 and onstream in 2030 (as reported).

news.headline: Leaked state assessments warn of irreversible Browse impacts ahead of federal decision
news.summary: Documents from Western Australian agencies warn of serious, irreversible risks to Scott Reef from Browse as the federal environment minister's decision is described as imminent.

news.headline: Colombia orders programmed gas rationing while SPEC repairs one of four regas trains
news.source: Colombia Ministry of Mines and Energy
news.summary: Ministry resolution caps the terminal at about 400 million cubic feet/day for an estimated 7 to 8 days of corrective work; rationing lifts only on official declaration.

news.headline: QatarEnergy extends force majeure on Italian LNG deliveries to end-December
news.summary: Edison received a new QatarEnergy force majeure notice covering Adriatic LNG deliveries until end-December, extending the earlier notice; Qatari supply stays constrained as the first expansion train nears start-up.

news.headline: Colombia orders fresh gas rationing after new fault at the SPEC Cartagena FSRU
news.summary: One of four regasification trains on the FSRU is under repair; terminal capped at about 400 million cubic feet/day for an estimated 7-8 days; second rationing since 25 September.

news.headline: Egypt grants tax exemption for the Aphrodite export pipeline; parliamentary ratification still pending
news.summary: Fiscal regime agreement exempts the midstream company from taxes other than income tax on sales to EGAS; needs Egyptian parliament approval; gas sales agreement with EGAS still under negotiation.

news.headline: Iraqi prime minister visits Amman; nine cooperation documents signed, pipeline remains a proposal
news.summary: Visit on 26 October produced memoranda on trade, energy and security but no pipeline agreement; Jordan's Iraqi crude imports by truck have been suspended since late 2025.

news.headline: Eni signs 1.8 billion dollar Kronos contracts, routing Cypriot gas to Egypt for export
news.summary: Eni awarded contracts worth about 1.8 billion dollars (as reported) to develop Kronos via Zohr infrastructure to Damietta LNG, first gas targeted 2028, reinforcing the Egypt-based virtual EastMed route.

news.headline: Galp says Venus fiscal talks are in the final stage and contractors are chosen
news.summary: Galp told analysts the Venus tax negotiations with Namibia are nearly closed, engineering contractors are selected and it is aligned with TotalEnergies on moving to a final investment decision.

news.headline: Egypt stayed the top destination for US LNG cargoes in August
news.summary: US Department of Energy monthly data show Egypt's floating import terminals were the largest single destination for US LNG for a third straight month in August.

news.headline: Summit FSRU terminal in Bangladesh passes 300 ship-to-ship transfers
news.summary: Summit LNG's floating terminal at Moheshkhali completed its 300th ship-to-ship LNG transfer since starting in 2019, a sign of steady throughput.

news.headline: EACOP reported 91 percent complete with control systems due mid-December
news.summary: Pipeline put at 91 percent complete (as reported) with electrical, metering and telecom systems targeted for mid-December 2026 before crude can be received.

news.headline: Ugandan official says first oil is weeks away with Kingfisher ready and Tilenga still drilling
news.summary: Kingfisher processing facility and well pads are reported ready while Tilenga is roughly three quarters built; the official first-oil window remains before end of June 2027.

news.headline: Pan American Energy chief: Hilli arrives June 2027, second floating unit Esperanza in 2028
news.summary: Hilli Episeyo is due in Argentina June 2027 with production from around September and commercial exports late 2027; the second unit, named Esperanza, arrives 2028 and starts 2029 (as reported).

news.headline: Turkmengaz targets Herat section completion by end-2026 and first gas mid-2027
news.summary: Turkmengaz chairman said the Serhetabat to Herat section should be built by end-2026 with first deliveries to Afghanistan by mid-2027, subject to Afghan readiness; volumes not yet fixed.

news.headline: HPCL says Rajasthan refinery runs at about 60 percent, full rate targeted by March 2027
news.summary: HPCL puts the refinery at roughly 60 percent utilisation (as reported), aiming for full capacity in the quarter to March 2027, when the first petrochemical units also begin commissioning.

news.headline: Minister says Balikpapan refinery upgrade is 99 percent done but technical issues remain
news.summary: After a site visit the energy minister put the upgrade at 99 percent progress (as reported) with remaining technical obstacles being worked through with Pertamina; no full-operation date given.

news.headline: Woodfibre LNG about three quarters built, completion expected mid-2027
news.summary: Alongside an economic impact study, Woodfibre LNG said construction is roughly 75 percent complete (as reported) with completion expected in mid-2027.

news.headline: Egypt regasified LNG volumes fell in August, imports back below domestic output
news.summary: MEES reports Egypt's gas imports dropped about 9 percent in August and regasified LNG fell versus July, putting imports back under domestic production (figures need verification).

news.headline: Wilhelmshaven 1 send-out to stop from 26 October for short planned maintenance
news.summary: Operator notice: Hoegh Esperanza halts send-out from 26 October for a few days of maintenance, timed after Excelsior at Wilhelmshaven 2 returns; reconnection expected end-October.

news.headline: Iraq LNG import start now tied to end of US-Iran conflict; Excelerate says work resumes as conditions allow
news.summary: Construction on Iraq's first floating import terminal is disrupted by the regional conflict; initial contract 240 mmcf/d expandable to 400 (ministry figure, verify).

news.headline: Energos Force cooled down ahead of Stade terminal commissioning
news.summary: Operator says the FSRU Energos Force has been cooled down as the final step before commissioning at Stade; no first-gas date given in the notice.

news.headline: Second outlet confirms Petrosen end-2027 FID target for Yakaar-Teranga
news.summary: African Energy Week round-up repeats that Petrosen is targeting a final investment decision on Yakaar-Teranga by the end of 2027.

news.headline: Venus sanction still hostage to Namibian fiscal and gas terms; 2027 slip now openly discussed
news.summary: Report says all major Venus bids are in but FID waits on fiscal and gas-monetisation terms; FID may land late 2026 or slip to 2027, putting 2030 first oil at risk. Single outlet.

news.headline: Pakistan takes second Qatari cargo of October as Engro terminal regas resumes
news.summary: Second contracted Qatari cargo now feeding the grid; first cargo berthed at Engro's terminal on 14 October after the QatarEnergy force majeure period.

news.headline: Azerbaijan supplied Syria 864 million cubic metres of gas in January to August 2026
news.summary: Official statistics put deliveries via Turkey at 864 million cubic metres worth about 295 million dollars (as reported); flows feed Aleppo and Homs plants, 1.2 bcm/year first phase.

news.headline: Afghan Herat section of TAPI about 80 percent built, commissioning by end-2026
news.summary: Pipeline company chief says the Serhetabat-Herat segment is about 80 percent complete and due for commissioning by end-2026; no timeline for Pakistan (as reported).

news.headline: Gaz-System completes jetty piling for the Gdansk FSRU terminal; commissioning kept at early 2028
news.summary: More than 500 steel piles driven for the jetty, reported on time and on budget; pipeline microtunnel finished; FSRU being outfitted in Ulsan for early-2028 commissioning.

news.headline: Scarborough reported 99 percent complete with first LNG still guided for fourth quarter 2026
news.summary: Woodside's third-quarter update keeps first LNG in the fourth quarter of 2026 after commissioning resumed following protests; completion figure as reported, needs verification.

news.headline: Mozambique cabinet reaffirms the 2019 sovereign guarantee backing Mozambique LNG lenders
news.summary: Council of Ministers reconfirmed the existing guarantee on 20 October with no new commitment or disclosed terms; first production still targeted for 2029.

news.headline: Taranaki LNG import terminal becomes a 7 November election issue
news.summary: Explainer notes the preferred provider is still unnamed and that Labour, Greens and Opportunity oppose the terminal, so the 7 November election likely decides whether it proceeds.

news.headline: Offshore Engineer: fiscal deal signed, Shell stake sale to MOL pending
news.summary: Report lists partners Chevron 35, Shell 35, NewMed 30 percent, notes the 15-year EGAS gas-sales term sheet from April and Shell's pending sale of its Cyprus stake to MOL.

news.headline: Southern Energy targets Hilli arrival June 2027 and commercial exports October 2027
news.summary: Company CEO says Hilli Episeyo arrives off Rio Negro in June 2027, four months of commissioning, commercial exports from October 2027; second unit 2028 (as reported).

news.headline: Trion 71 percent complete with offshore installation under way
news.summary: Production unit 96 percent fabricated, first subsea tree installed, 10 of 24 wells drilled; first oil still targeted 2028 (as reported).

news.headline: Law of the Sea tribunal sets November hearing on Argentina bid to halt Sea Lion
news.summary: Tribunal fixed a 10-11 November Hamburg hearing on Argentina's 13 October provisional-measures request; the order itself does not suspend the project.

news.headline: TotalEnergies calls Venus sanction-ready with contractor bids in hand
news.summary: FPSO, subsea and drilling offers received; FID still hinges on commercial terms with Namibia, first oil around 2030 (as reported).

news.headline: Louisiana LNG 32 percent complete, steel supply disrupted, first LNG still 2029
news.summary: Train 1 at 41 percent, train 3 first concrete poured; structural steel delays from Middle East disruption being mitigated; first LNG 2029 (as reported).

news.headline: Pluto train 2 at 99 percent with Scarborough gas introduced to warm end
news.summary: All compressor mechanical runs complete, cold-end work continues before liquefaction; first LNG cargo targeted Q4 2026 (as reported).

news.headline: Woodside puts Scarborough at 99 percent complete, first cargo still fourth quarter 2026
news.summary: Reservoir gas exported into the trunkline and reached the LNG train warm end; project on budget, first LNG cargo on track for Q4 2026 (as reported).

news.headline: Egypt and Chevron initial Aphrodite fiscal agreement; pipeline tariff still disputed
news.summary: Fiscal regime agreement initialled at MOC 2026 but transport tariff for the Egyptian leg is contested; NewMed now shows FID 2028 and first gas 2031 per the report.

news.headline: Nusantara Regas Satu logs 33 cargoes and 96 percent availability through September
news.summary: Nusantara Regas reports 33 LNG cargoes received and 96 percent FSRU availability through the third quarter of 2026 (figures as reported, need verification).

news.headline: UNOC says pipeline over 98 percent complete, first oil around June 2027
news.summary: UNOC official at Africa Energy Week: line ready to receive crude by end-2026, first oil expected around June 2027, peak 246,000 barrels/day (as reported).

news.headline: Qatar plan would build two 825 megawatt plants at Deir Ammar and Zahrani with 20-year LNG deal
news.summary: Draft programme seen by Reuters: two combined-cycle plants over about three years, 20-year QatarEnergy LNG deal and a 3.5 million cubic metres/day FSRU; approvals pending.

news.headline: Jordan's king and Iraq's president push for Basra-Aqaba pipeline
news.summary: Phone call stressed moving ahead with the Hormuz-bypassing line; recap of 1,700 km, 1 million barrels/day, about 18 billion dollars (as reported); still unimplemented.

news.headline: Egypt and Chevron initial fiscal framework with 4 billion dollar plan and 800 mmcf/d facility
news.summary: Fiscal framework initialled at MOC 2026; plan put at about 4 billion dollars with a floating production facility up to 800 million cubic feet/day and subsea line to Egypt (as reported).

news.headline: TotalEnergies lines up three-well Mopane campaign, FID targeted 2028
news.summary: Three-well exploration and appraisal campaign on the Tungsten Explorer drillship planned from second half 2026; FID targeted 2028 (as reported).

news.headline: Tanga confirmed as export terminus, UNOC floats Tanga energy hub
news.summary: Pipeline ending at Tanga to be ready for crude by end-2026 with first exports around June 2027; UNOC plans a Tanga hub with a products line back to Uganda.

news.headline: Greek LNG imports rise in January to September, Alexandroupolis included
news.summary: Deliveries to Revithoussa and the Alexandroupolis floating terminal rose over the first nine months of 2026, with the United States the main supplier; volumes paywalled.

news.headline: Gaz-System advances jetty construction for first Gdansk FSRU
news.summary: Jetty works for the first floating unit at Gdansk are moving ahead; detail is paywalled, no new start-up date stated.

news.headline: Review still cites phased 2026 commissioning for AKK despite operator delay complaints
news.summary: Secondary review says the line has reached Abuja and is being commissioned in phases targeted for 2026; conflicts with primary reports of delay, so treat with caution.

news.headline: Industry review records Algerian segment construction start, Niger transit still the hurdle
news.summary: Secondary review states Sonatrach launched construction of the Algerian section in June 2026 and names Niger security and financing as the open risks. Not fresh primary news.

news.headline: Review: treaty signed, but 25 billion dollar financing and shippers still missing for Nigeria-Morocco line
news.summary: Same review notes ECOWAS leaders signed the pipeline treaty in July 2026; financing of about 25 billion dollars (as reported) and binding offtake remain outstanding.

news.headline: Analyst says Aphrodite FID may slip to 2028 amid tariff row and Israel dispute
news.summary: NewMed reportedly now guides FID in 2028 (was early 2027); Chevron will not sanction until the Cyprus-Israel reservoir dispute is settled; last week's talks failed.

news.headline: Three Aphrodite agreements slated for signing at MOC 2026 in Alexandria
news.summary: Fiscal regime, gas sales and purchase, and gas transportation agreements between Chevron, EGAS and the petroleum ministry were scheduled for 20-22 October; a 280 km subsea link to Egypt is planned.

news.headline: Cyprus government tells parliament Vasilikos LNG terminal will not run before 2030
news.summary: Energy minister told MPs the terminal is expected operational by 2030; completion tender to be awarded before summer 2027 with work starting in second half 2027. Prometheas still in Malaysia.

news.headline: Woodside resumes Scarborough FPU commissioning after Greenpeace occupation
news.summary: Woodside said commissioning of the Scarborough floating production unit offshore Western Australia resumed after Greenpeace activists occupied it; no schedule impact stated.

news.headline: Cyprus and Aphrodite partners at odds over Egypt transit tariff
news.summary: Partners reportedly raised the tariff for the Egyptian-waters pipeline section to about 3 dollars/mmBtu from about 1; Nicosia wants a better offer; FID within 2027, first gas 2031.

news.headline: SPEC Cartagena terminal to lift sendout to 533 million cubic feet/day by 2027
news.summary: Expansion from 475 to 533 million cubic feet/day by 2027 with investment above 60 million dollars; 450 reserved for power (as reported, needs verification).

news.headline: MEES: virtual EastMed via Egypt gains backing over the 2,000 km pipeline
news.summary: Corridor using short subsea links to Egypt, existing liquefaction and LNG shipping, backed at the 7 October Athens forum, is displacing the original pipeline concept.

news.headline: Cypriot gas to Europe via Egypt instead of a dedicated pipeline, analysis says
news.summary: Cronos gas (500 mmcf/d from March 2028, as reported) would flow to Zohr infrastructure and Damietta LNG, with Egypt keeping up to 20 percent; no subsea line to Greece.

news.headline: Eight contractors seek to finish Vasilikos terminal; remaining works put at about 180 million euros
news.summary: Eight firms including Saipem, China Harbour, Petrojet, Terna and Archirodon expressed interest by the 9 October deadline; remaining works reported at about 180 million euros (needs verification).

news.headline: Petrosen pushes Yakaar-Teranga investment decision to end-2027 while hunting partners
news.summary: At African Energy Week, Petrosen said FID is now targeted by end-2027; phase one cited at about 2.5 billion dollars (as reported, needs verification).

news.headline: Subsea cable delivered for Klaipeda FSRU shore-power link due May 2028
news.summary: KN Energies received the 3.88 km subsea cable to connect FSRU Independence to shore power; full project due May 2028, cutting terminal emissions by about a third.

news.headline: Senegal seeks new partners for Yakaar-Teranga after Kosmos exit
news.summary: Energy minister says Petrosen holds the field since Kosmos left in April and the state wants investor partners; 104 blocks also on offer (as reported).

news.headline: New Zealand names preferred Port Taranaki FSRU provider but no contract before election
news.summary: Ministry wording now says a preferred provider is shortlisted (unnamed); no signing before the 7 November election; target still operation by winter 2028.

news.headline: TotalEnergies and Namibia still negotiating Venus terms as 2026 FID target nears
news.summary: Terms for the roughly 160 thousand barrels/day project remain under negotiation; Namibian presidency would not say whether FID lands this year, leaving the 2030 first-oil target under pressure.

news.headline: Cyprus relaunches tender to finish Vasilikos terminal; eight parties interested, Prometheas still uncertified
news.summary: Defa targets preselection by end-2026 and award before summer 2027; minister estimates two years to complete; FSRU Prometheas remains uncertified in Malaysia.

news.headline: Pakistan LNG terminals running intermittently under Qatar force majeure; Engro unit restarts after month-long shutdown
news.summary: Engro terminal restarted 13 October after being shut since 26 September; Pakistan GasPort unit idle since 9 October. Only two cargoes expected in October as QatarEnergy force majeure runs to 6 November.

news.headline: Aramco outlines gas build-out at World Petroleum Congress, Jafurah central to plan
news.summary: Aramco plans up to seven gas facilities by 2027 and says Jafurah, producing since December 2025, targets 2 billion cubic feet/day by 2030.

news.headline: DET starts maintenance at second Wilhelmshaven FSRU terminal
news.summary: Deutsche Energy Terminal has begun maintenance at its second Wilhelmshaven floating terminal; duration not given in the free text.

news.headline: TotalEnergies sets out local spending and jobs pledge for Venus ahead of FID
news.summary: TotalEnergies cites about N$33 billion in local procurement, roughly 5,000 jobs and a US$50 million social programme that would start after FID; no FID date given.

news.headline: Hanseatic Energy Hub offers more long-term capacity at Stade
news.summary: HEH plans to market additional long-term regasification capacity at the onshore Stade terminal ahead of start-up.

news.headline: First North Field East train ready in November, production seen first quarter 2027
news.summary: Sources say the first expansion train will be ready to run in November with output in 1Q 2027; two damaged Ras Laffan trains stay offline for years.

news.headline: Private gas group presses NNPC over repeated pipeline delays
news.summary: A compressed natural gas industry alliance asked NNPC to explain missed deadlines; full completion is now projected to slip into 2027.

news.headline: Algeria says its section of the Trans-Saharan pipeline is under construction
news.summary: Algeria's hydrocarbons minister said studies are done, the Algerian section is being built and early pipe-laying has begun in Niger. Capacity 20 to 30 billion cubic metres/year.

news.headline: Piombino council files objection in Snam terminal review
news.summary: The municipality filed a negative opinion in the environmental review. Documents consider operation for up to 22 to 25 years; no extension has been approved.

news.headline: Kudu power transmission licence held up by Namibia policy gap
news.summary: BW Kudu's transmission licence is on hold until a framework for private transmission exists. NamPower objected. Plant size restated at 420 megawatts.

news.headline: Uganda first oil now expected by end-June 2027, pipeline ready by December
news.summary: A Ugandan parliament committee chair said the pipeline will be ready for crude by mid-December 2026 and first oil is expected before end-June 2027.

news.headline: Cyprus puts cost to finish Vasilikos terminal at about 180 million euros

news.headline: LNG Hrvatska chief sets out 2027 capacity auction and possible further expansion
news.summary: Interview: a 2027 auction will offer 4.5 billion cubic metres of capacity; a sell-out could trigger another expansion. Figures as reported.

news.headline: Valve supply contract awarded for Ruwais LNG trains
news.summary: AMPO Poyam Valves will supply more than 600 cryogenic ball valves for the two electric-drive trains. Capacity restated at 9.6 million tonnes/year.

news.headline: Korean officials say no investment agreed for Alaska LNG
news.summary: After a US announcement of 50 billion dollars of Korean backing, Korean officials told Alaska lawmakers nothing is agreed and any money follows a final investment decision.

news.headline: Deadline closes for firms wanting to finish the stalled Vasilikos LNG terminal
news.summary: Expressions of interest closed 9 October. Completion is put at about EUR 180 million and two years (reported, needs verification). The vessel is still in Malaysia.

news.headline: Shell to take 30 percent of Bay du Nord; decision due early 2027, first oil 2031
news.summary: Equinor keeps 70 percent and operatorship. Investment about CAD 14 billion, over 400 million barrels in phase one (company figures, need verification).

news.headline: Six groups reported interested in completing Vasilikos; Cyfield in talks with China Harbour
news.summary: Local press names China Harbour, Saipem, Terna, Avax, Archirodon and ECOnnect Energy as interested. ETYFA will shortlist before inviting full offers.

news.headline: Hilli Episeyo being prepared in Singapore for Argentina, operations late 2027

news.headline: Larsen and Toubro reported to lead bidding for Jafurah phase 5 compression plants
news.summary: Phase 5 covers three compression plants; no award announced. Article says first Jafurah gas came in December 2025. Single outlet.

news.headline: First North Field East train reported ready to start in November

news.headline: Export buoys arrive for Vaca Muerta Oil Sur terminal

news.headline: Romanian government and OMV say Neptun Deep is on schedule for 2027 production
news.summary: The interim prime minister met OMV's new chief executive on 5 October. The government said the project is on the agreed schedule with production next year.

news.headline: Olmeca refinery running at about three quarters of capacity
news.summary: Pemex data show about 252,000 barrels/day of crude processed in August 2026, 74 percent of capacity. Article says commercial operations began August 2024.

news.summary: President Tebboune said survey and security preparation is under way in Algeria and Niger. No completion date or cost given. Figure as reported, needs verification.

news.headline: Three bidders compete to build Egypt's first onshore LNG regasification terminal
news.summary: BGN of Turkey, UCC Holding of Qatar and a local player. Initial capacity about 1 billion cubic feet/day.

news.headline: Dredging under way for Iraq's first LNG import terminal
news.summary: Five-year regasification and supply deal with extension options and a minimum contracted offtake.

news.headline: Floating gas terminal deal agreed for Khor al-Zubair
news.summary: Project set to proceed after a meeting between the prime minister and Excelerate Energy.

news.headline: Excelerate Energy delays Iraq's first LNG import terminal until 2027

news.summary: Gasunie and Vopak took a conditional decision to run the terminal beyond 2027 with two Exmar units.
